static_findings: quality.sh has only an EXIT trap; finish reads $? and otherwise retains run_status=0. A signal can terminate the shell while the last completed command status remains 0.
run_check immediately snapshots PIPESTATUS for timeout and tee after its foreground pipeline; this preserves ordinary failures and timeout status if control returns normally.

Bash may defer INT/TERM traps while waiting for foreground pipeline completion. GNU timeout creates a separate process group by default, so signaling the Bash process group may not reach the timeout child group.
A minimal explicit INT/TERM exit130/143 trap should make EXIT recording nonzero, but does not itself forward signals or clean child groups.
